description: Has no side effects (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`). Crawlers, prefetchers and caches may call it at will.
Repeating it has the same effect as sending it once (`GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE`). Makes automatic retries safe. `POST` is not.
Request header with a client-generated key; the server stores the result per key so a retried `POST` is not executed twice.
Response header that decides who may store a response and for how long: `public`, `private`, `max-age`, `no-store`, `immutable`.
A version identifier of a response. The client sends `If-None-Match`; the server answers `304 Not Modified` without a body when unchanged.
`OPTIONS` request the browser sends before cross-origin requests with JSON bodies, custom headers or non-simple methods.
`401`: not authenticated (missing or invalid credentials). `403`: authenticated but not allowed.
